cards.definition_principle: Delta, Gamma, Theta, Vega, and Rho estimate sensitivity to pricing inputs; they do not guarantee exact realized premium changes.
measurable_predicates: Greek source timestamp is within freshness policy
realized quote is kept separate from model estimate
valid_conditions: Greeks are presented as sensitivities with current input lineage.
failure_conditions: A stale or missing Greek is inferred, or a model estimate is reported as executable price.
contradictions: Changing volatility, time, price, rates, or dividends can change the sensitivities.
when_not_to_use: Do not call Delta a CITADEL probability or use one Greek as contract authorization.
cards.short_excerpt: Greeks are not a guarantee of exact option premium changes
cards.paraphrase: Use Greeks to explain sensitivity, then verify actual premium and liquidity from current quotes.

cards.definition_principle: Premium response depends on underlying price, strike, time to expiry, implied volatility, rates, dividends, and executable market conditions; direction alone is insufficient.
measurable_predicates: pricing inputs and bid/ask share an atomic freshness boundary
valid_conditions: The exact option contract and quote are fresh.
failure_conditions: Contract identity, IV, expiry, or executable quote is stale or unavailable.
contradictions: A favorable underlying move may not offset time decay, IV change, or spread.
when_not_to_use: Do not use as standalone direction, confidence, or probability.
cards.paraphrase: Require a fresh contract-specific option lane; underlying direction alone cannot prove premium capture.

cards.definition_principle: Delta describes modeled premium sensitivity to underlying price and changes with price and time; it is not a fixed percentage.
measurable_predicates: delta belongs to exact contract snapshot
underlying and option timestamps are aligned
valid_conditions: Delta is used as a contract sensitivity bucket, not outcome probability.
failure_conditions: Delta is stale, cross-contract, or converted into a win probability.
contradictions: Gamma, time, volatility, and liquidity can change realized response.
when_not_to_use: Do not select a contract from Delta alone.
cards.exact_locator: Volatility and the Greeks > Delta paragraph
cards.short_excerpt: The Delta is not a fixed percentage
cards.paraphrase: Use fresh Delta as one dynamic sensitivity feature within exact-contract evidence.

cards.definition_principle: Gamma measures how Delta changes as the underlying changes, so option directional sensitivity is nonlinear and can move quickly.
measurable_predicates: gamma and delta timestamps match the quote snapshot
valid_conditions: Gamma is disclosed as a modeled local sensitivity.
failure_conditions: Gamma is missing or treated as a deterministic future hedge flow.
contradictions: Aggregate dealer Gamma exposure and dealer positioning are not observed by a single-contract Greek.
when_not_to_use: Do not infer GEX regime or dealer direction from contract Gamma alone.
cards.exact_locator: Volatility and the Greeks > Gamma paragraph
cards.paraphrase: Disclose changing sensitivity without inventing dealer-position or GEX causality.

cards.concept: Theta makes timing part of option buying
cards.definition_principle: Theta represents modeled premium sensitivity to time, is not constant, and can accelerate near expiry; option-buying evidence needs an explicit holding window.
measurable_predicates: expiry and observation time determine time remaining
theta belongs to exact contract snapshot
valid_conditions: The option thesis has a bounded time window.
failure_conditions: Theta or expiry is missing, or the setup has no time invalidation.
contradictions: Realized premium decay is not guaranteed to equal the model sensitivity.
when_not_to_use: Do not compare contracts across expiries without normalizing time context.
cards.exact_locator: Volatility and the Greeks > Theta paragraph
cards.short_excerpt: Theta values are not constant and accelerate as expiration approaches
cards.paraphrase: Require expiry-aware timing and disclose model/realized differences.

cards.concept: Vega and implied volatility can oppose direction
cards.definition_principle: Vega estimates premium sensitivity to implied volatility; a drop in IV can reduce premium even when the underlying moves in the expected direction.
measurable_predicates: vega and IV belong to exact contract
pre/post IV and premium are timestamped
valid_conditions: IV and premium response are compared on the same contract.
failure_conditions: IV is unavailable or contracts are mixed across snapshots.
contradictions: Vega is a local modeled sensitivity; realized response may differ.
when_not_to_use: Do not call IV change directional confirmation.
cards.exact_locator: Volatility and the Greeks > Vega paragraph
cards.paraphrase: Test premium confirmation directly and treat Vega/IV as explanatory sensitivity.

cards.definition_principle: An option holder can lose the full premium; every long-option explanation must retain costs, expiry, and invalidation rather than imply guaranteed capture.
measurable_predicates: maximum premium at risk is explicit
failure_conditions: Risk, costs, expiry, or stop mapping is omitted.
contradictions: No principle or Greek establishes a guaranteed profitable response.
when_not_to_use: Do not convert the general loss boundary into setup probability.
cards.exact_locator: What are some of the risks associated with trading options? > option holders paragraph
cards.short_excerpt: Option holders risk the entire amount of the premium paid
cards.paraphrase: Keep full-premium loss possible and require explicit time, cost, and invalidation evidence.
